DOI:10.1136/archdischild-2022-nppg.45.topic: Excipients in unlicensed paediatric liquid medicines
DOI:10.1136/archdischild-2022-nppg.45.standard: European Medicines Agency guidelines on excipients; acceptable daily intake (ADI) of each excipient, assessed with the local New Products Assessment Form

cycle1.result: 14 unlicensed liquid preparations from one manufacturer reviewed: 4/14 (29%) suitable for all age groups; 4/14 (29%) exceeded the ADI for an excipient in neonates (suitable for all other ages); 5/14 (36%) changed to a more appropriate alternative.

DOI:10.1136/archdischild-2022-nppg.45.other_findings: Of the four exceeding ADI in neonates, two were not routinely prescribed in neonates; one preparation was removed from the market. Manufacturer was asked to reformulate where ADI was exceeded.

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keaf142.013.topic: Time to diagnosis in axial spondyloarthritis
DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keaf142.013.setting: 54 UK rheumatology departments; national online survey-based audit run by the National Axial Spondyloarthritis Society
DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keaf142.013.standard: NASS 'Act on Axial SpA' campaign target to reduce time to diagnosis to 12 months

cycle1.dates: Survey launched October 2022; patients diagnosed January 2021 to September 2024
cycle1.result: Mean total time to diagnosis 8 years (SD 8.91); median 4.7 years (IQR 9.25).

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keaf142.013.other_findings: Preliminary data suggest a trend towards shorter time to diagnosis, apparently from quicker primary care referral and faster rheumatology assessment. Men had shorter time to diagnosis, but improvement between 2021 and 2024 was greater for women.

DOI:10.1136/archdischild-2023-nppg.14.setting: Tertiary centre; paediatric patients (>30 days and <17 years) receiving intravenous vancomycin
DOI:10.1136/archdischild-2023-nppg.14.standard: Local trust guideline (2018) for intravenous vancomycin in children

cycle1.result: Correct frequency 75.9%; correct first dose 58.6%; concentrations taken at correct time 89.7%; therapeutic first concentration 24.1% (70.4% under range); second concentration in range 61.9%.

DOI:10.1136/archdischild-2023-nppg.14.intervention: Significant changes to electronic prescription and concentration report templates; guideline recirculated to all paediatric prescribers.

cycle2.result: Correct frequency 92.6%; correct first dose 71.4%; concentrations taken at correct time 96.2%; therapeutic first concentration 19.2% (65.4% under range); second concentration in range 57.9%.

DOI:10.1136/archdischild-2023-nppg.14.other_findings: Non-compliance with prescribing was due to prescribers following BNFC rather than trust guidance. Therapeutic concentrations were still not achieved in over 80% of patients, prompting a call to re-evaluate the dosing guideline.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.584.setting: Community Adult Mental Health Services, Taylor Centre, Southend; outpatient clinics
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.584.standard: NICE CG178 1.5.8 (offer supported employment to people with psychosis or schizophrenia who wish to work) and NG181 1.8.9 (facilitate alternative educational or occupational activities)

cycle1.result: Supported employment offered to 35% of the non-working sample; alternative educational or occupational options offered to 26%.

cycle2.result: Employment status documented in 97%; supported employment offered to 38%; alternative educational or employment options offered to 47%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.584.other_findings: 64% of those offered supported employment declined; 78% were not actively seeking work. Only 33% were followed up, and employment was most often discussed at follow-up appointments (87%).

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11685.topic: Physical health monitoring in early intervention in psychosis
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11685.setting: Mid and North Early Intervention in Psychosis service, Hampshire and Isle of Wight NHS Foundation Trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11685.standard: Physical health monitoring and intervention standards of the National Audit of Schizophrenia 2021 and National Clinical Audit of Psychosis 2022 (75% standard); Lester UK tool; local target 80% after interventions

cycle1.result: 54/118 identified as high risk. Monitoring of smoking, alcohol, illicit substances, BMI, blood pressure, lipids and glucose exceeded the 75% standard. Acceptance of interventions was low: smoking cessation 18%, alcohol interventions 33%, illicit substance advice 6%, HbA1c-related recommendations 8%, lipid lifestyle advice 10%; 100% accepted interventions for high BMI and hypertension.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11685.other_findings: Standards for monitoring were met but not for interventions; an action plan (patient education and team training on Lester tool interventions) was recommended before the next cycle, with re-audit every 6 months.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znab117.081.setting: Acute hospitals in the UK and Ireland; national trainee collaborative (protocol)
DOI:10.1093/bjs/znab117.081.standard: WHO Mastitis Guidelines 2000; GAIN Guidelines 2008; ABM Clinical Protocol #4: Mastitis 2014; NICE Clinical Knowledge Summaries: Mastitis and Breast Abscess

cycle1.result: not reported

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znab117.081.other_findings: Protocol only: planned three phases (national practice survey, prospective audit, prospective re-audit) collecting antibiotic prescribing, operative versus radiological management, time to ultrasound, inpatient versus outpatient treatment, length of stay and breast surgeon follow-up.

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keae163.020.topic: Serious infections in early inflammatory arthritis
DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keae163.020.setting: National Early Inflammatory Arthritis Audit (NEIAA), England; observational cohort with NHS Digital linkage

cycle1.result: 519 serious infection admissions and 17 deaths; incidence per 100 person-years 3.19 (95% CI 2.93-3.48) for admissions and 0.10 (0.06-0.16) for deaths. MTX-based strategies HR 0.75 and csDMARD combination HR 0.70 versus no DMARD; each 1-unit DAS28 rise HR 1.08.

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keae163.020.other_findings: Age, smoking, comorbidity, disease activity, symptom burden and disability predicted admissions; corticosteroid association was not significant in fully adjusted models.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.400.standard: Patients detained under the MHA should have Section 17 leave facilitated as granted by the responsible clinician, with documented discussion and updated risk assessment before leave

cycle1.result: Section 17 form not uploaded to RIO in 25% (7); no documented discussion of leave in 46.42% (13); no evidence whether leave facilitated in 25% (7); 42% (6) of those granted leave off grounds had it facilitated; no updated risk assessment before leave in 83% (5/6).

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.400.other_findings: All facilitated leave was escorted as specified. Recommendations: discuss leave at ward rounds and one-to-one sessions, document risk assessment and use the pre-leave form; re-audit after 12 months.

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keac133.292.topic: Tocilizumab approval criteria in giant cell arteritis
DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keac133.292.setting: Bristol and Bath regional GCA multidisciplinary team meeting
DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keac133.292.standard: NHS England criteria (Blueteq) for tocilizumab in refractory or relapsing GCA; MDT discussion required before starting

cycle1.result: 38 cases discussed, 31 approved for tocilizumab; 100% of approved cases met criteria for refractory (n = 11) or relapsing (n = 20) disease.

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keac133.292.other_findings: High glucocorticoid toxicity burden; 77.4% cranial GCA, 48.4% large vessel, 25.8% ischaemic visual loss. Patients with ocular involvement were referred earlier (478.2 vs 648.1 days).

DOI:10.1136/archdischild-2020-nppg.58.topic: Vitamin D testing in paediatric haematology and oncology
DOI:10.1136/archdischild-2020-nppg.58.setting: Paediatric haematology/oncology; new diagnoses of malignant disease
DOI:10.1136/archdischild-2020-nppg.58.standard: Trust guideline for vitamin D deficiency: 100% tested at diagnosis; 100% of results acted on; 100% given appropriate dose

cycle1.result: 56% tested for vitamin D during admission; 35% of oncology and 83% of haematology patients tested. 6% of haematology and 5% of oncology patients with sufficient levels received treatment not indicated; the 5% of oncology patients with insufficient levels were not treated. Standards not met.

DOI:10.1136/archdischild-2020-nppg.58.other_findings: Recommendations: follow the revised trust guideline, pharmacists to check vitamin D for all new admissions, and build a default test into the new prescribing system.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afaf368.022.topic: Bone health assessment after inpatient falls
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afaf368.022.setting: Sherwood Forest Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust (Kings Mill Hospital); inpatients who fell, identified via DATIX
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afaf368.022.standard: National Osteoporosis Guideline Group: FRAX to estimate 10-year fracture risk and guide bone protection; NICE CG161; Trust post-fall assessment guidance

cycle1.result: Falls assessment sheet completed in over 80%; FRAX calculated in only 33.3%. Of those with FRAX, 60% intermediate, 20% high and 10% very high risk; only 50% of high-risk patients received oral bisphosphonates. Retrospective FRAX in those not assessed showed 60% very high risk.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afaf368.022.other_findings: Calcium and vitamin D checks were done more often than FRAX but still below optimal; renal impairment limited bisphosphonate eligibility. Falls Alert Stickers with checkboxes and QR code, a revised post-falls proforma with a bone health section, and clinician education were introduced.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10683.setting: Outpatient department, Punjab Institute of Mental Health, Lahore
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10683.standard: Maudsley Prescribing Guidelines (14th edition) for long-acting injectable antipsychotics

cycle1.result: All patients on fluphenazine decanoate with a concurrent second antipsychotic (100% polypharmacy); 78% informed of side effects; none had post-injection observation; no test doses given; no baseline ECG or physical health assessment; fluphenazine used in rapid tranquillisation.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10683.other_findings: Recommendations included staff training on Maudsley guidance, test dose protocols, mandatory baseline ECG, revised rapid tranquillisation protocol and regular re-audit.

DOI:10.1136/archdischild-2023-nppg.1.standard: Trust guideline: Labinic probiotic for babies <32 weeks and/or <1.5 kg at birth, at correct dose, given with first feed or within 12 hours of birth

cycle1.result: 76/76 (100%) eligible babies prescribed and given Labinic; 76/76 (100%) correct dose; only 17/76 (22%) received it within the first 12 hours.

DOI:10.1136/archdischild-2023-nppg.1.other_findings: Unit went from 0% to 100% of eligible babies receiving probiotics after the GIRFT recommendation. Planned nurse education, updated guidance and e-prescribing to stress first dose within 12 hours, and re-audit.

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keab247.020.topic: COVID-19 outcomes in shielded rheumatology patients
DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keab247.020.setting: Mid and South Essex NHS Foundation Trust and Barking, Havering and Redbridge University Hospitals NHS Trust rheumatology departments

cycle1.result: 28/5876 (0.48%) shielded patients hospitalised with COVID-19 (23/4914, 0.47% MSE; 5/962, 0.52% BHR); 10/28 (36%) died. Shielded rheumatology patients were 0.76% (28/3695) of all COVID-19 admissions.

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keab247.020.other_findings: Admitted patients were mostly elderly with multiple comorbidities; only one was on anti-TNF therapy.

DOI:10.1136/archdischild-2020-nppg.47.topic: Antibiotic choice and duration in necrotising enterocolitis
DOI:10.1136/archdischild-2020-nppg.47.setting: Single UK tertiary children's hospital providing neonatal intensive care and neonatal surgery
DOI:10.1136/archdischild-2020-nppg.47.standard: Local NEC guideline: first-line amoxicillin, gentamicin and metronidazole for up to 10 days

cycle1.result: Guideline regimen (amoxicillin, gentamicin, metronidazole) used in 1/7; ceftazidime, vancomycin and metronidazole in 4; meropenem and vancomycin in 2. Median course 10 days (range 2 to 16).

DOI:10.1136/archdischild-2020-nppg.47.intervention: Results presented to a neonatal surgery quality improvement meeting in January 2019 to highlight the issue to surgical and neonatal teams.

cycle2.result: Guideline regimen used in 4/5; ceftazidime, vancomycin and metronidazole in 1. Median course 11 days (range 5 to 12).

DOI:10.1136/archdischild-2020-nppg.47.other_findings: Compliance with antibiotic choice improved but treatment duration still varied considerably.

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keab247.172.topic: Axial spondyloarthritis management against NICE QS170
DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keab247.172.setting: Royal National Hospital for Rheumatic Diseases, Bath; tertiary axSpA centre; patients starting bDMARDs
DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keab247.172.standard: NICE QS170 (MRI if no radiographic evidence, structured exercise programme, patient information) and clinical practice guidelines

cycle1.result: MRI in 18/19 (94.7%) with X-rays showing no sacroiliitis; education in 228/267 (85.4%); referral to structured exercise 217/259 (83.8%); first-line NSAIDs 246/248 (99.2%); 6-monthly renal monitoring on NSAIDs 80.3%; 12-week bDMARD response assessment 198/233 (85.0%).

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keab247.172.other_findings: 300 sampled from 539, 269 met inclusion. Median time from symptom onset to diagnosis 6.26 years.

DOI:10.1302/1358-992x.2023.16.011.topic: Postoperative care documentation in operation notes
DOI:10.1302/1358-992x.2023.16.011.setting: Spinal surgery, Sheffield Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
DOI:10.1302/1358-992x.2023.16.011.standard: MDT consensus of 15 essential criteria for complete post-operative care documentation (no published standard)

cycle1.result: Baseline: >75% compliance in 4 criteria and <50% compliance in 10 of 15 criteria.

DOI:10.1302/1358-992x.2023.16.011.intervention: Post-operative care template based on the 15 criteria embedded in existing IT software as a non-overwriting suffix needing two mouse clicks; later template update after a usage questionnaire.

cycle2.dates: 12 months after template update (5 years post baseline)

DOI:10.1302/1358-992x.2023.16.011.other_findings: Six audit cycles, >400 operation notes over 5 years: improvement sustained at 3 and 12 months, declined at 24 months (new staff unaware of template, response option problems), then >75% in 11 criteria after template update.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10101.setting: Marsden House CAMHS, Cheshire and Wirral Partnership NHS Foundation Trust; internal referrals to psychiatry
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10101.standard: Referral quality indicators (demographics, consent, prior therapy interventions per NICE, risk assessment)

cycle1.result: Mean 2.7/5 demographic identifiers; consent documented 43% (10/23); prior therapy documented 65% (15/23); risk mentioned 39% (9/23); mean 2.43 emails per referral.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10101.other_findings: Lack of a standardised referral form was the main cause; recommendations were a form with mandatory fields, referrer training and a streamlined process.

DOI:10.1136/heartjnl-2017-311726.3.topic: MRA and ICD therapy after myocardial infarction with LV dysfunction
DOI:10.1136/heartjnl-2017-311726.3.setting: Ulster Hospital, Dundonald; MI patients from MINAP database
DOI:10.1136/heartjnl-2017-311726.3.standard: MRA for eligible patients with post-MI LVEF ≤40% and heart failure or diabetes (EPHESUS); repeat LV imaging at 6-12 weeks and device therapy if LVEF ≤35% persists

cycle1.result: 47 (14%) eligible for MRA, 22 (47%) prescribed. 27 eligible for device consideration; 23 (85%) had repeat LV assessment (mean 107 days); 4 had ongoing severe LVSD, of whom 1 (25%) had an ICD.

DOI:10.1136/heartjnl-2017-311726.3.other_findings: Of those with ongoing severe LVSD, 25% died before review and 50% had no documented reason why device therapy was not considered.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10571.topic: Benzodiazepine and Z-drug prescribing in inpatient psychiatry
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10571.setting: Heddfan acute adult inpatient psychiatric unit, North Wales
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10571.standard: National guidelines on benzodiazepine and hypnotic treatment duration and dosage limits

cycle1.result: 38/40 prescribed PRN benzodiazepines (lorazepam 35/38, 92%); only 12/38 reviewed within a week; one had PRN stopped; half continued PRN benzodiazepines for more than 3 weeks. 20 (50%) received zopiclone, 66% (8) of these for 3 weeks or more.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10571.other_findings: 11 (27.5%) were already on regular benzodiazepines. Planned pharmacist-led weekly PRN review at ward rounds and a protocol for reducing and stopping PRN medication.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11479.setting: Two autism specialist rehabilitation wards (Springs Centre and Springs Wing), Cygnet Harrow Hospital

cycle1.result: Considerable proficiency across about 11 of 18 assessed domains; persistent deficits in six areas including autonomous decision-making, behavioural adaptation under stress, social cognition, transition preparedness, proprioception and motor planning.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11479.other_findings: Multidisciplinary assessment across 18 domains; findings to inform care planning and bespoke therapeutic pathways.

DOI:10.1136/archdischild-2023-nppg.27.topic: Liver function monitoring on CFTR modulators
DOI:10.1136/archdischild-2023-nppg.27.setting: Large tertiary paediatric cystic fibrosis centre; patients newly started on Kaftrio
DOI:10.1136/archdischild-2023-nppg.27.standard: Local trust guideline, SmPC and MHRA Drug Safety Update: baseline LFTs, then every 3 months in the first year; defined actions for raised ALT/AST

cycle1.result: Baseline LFTs 30/31 (97%); LFTs at 3 months 10/31 (32%) (15 too early, 6 late); 0 patients had four sets at correct 3-monthly intervals; 4 (13%) had abnormal LFTs, 50% of which were acted on per guidelines.

DOI:10.1136/archdischild-2023-nppg.27.other_findings: Rate of liver impairment was low; authors suggest reviewing whether local practice should deviate from national guidance to fit real-world practice.

DOI:10.1136/archdischild-2023-nppg.11.setting: Tertiary PICU and paediatric high dependency unit (Royal Brompton and Harefield guideline)
DOI:10.1136/archdischild-2023-nppg.11.standard: Local PICU analgesia and sedation guideline (2020): approved indication; dose not above 1.4 microgram/kg/hour; duration not above 72 hours

cycle1.result: 32/33 (97%) prescribed for approved indications; no patient exceeded 1.4 microgram/kg/hour; infusion exceeded 72 hours in 3 (9%).

DOI:10.1136/archdischild-2023-nppg.11.other_findings: COMFORT scores recorded for 15/18 non-extubation courses but none had documented target scores; guideline education and a monthly 'DRUGgle' update were delivered before and during data collection. Repeat audit planned.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11704.topic: Antipsychotic use for non-cognitive symptoms of dementia
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11704.setting: Southwest Crisis Function Team, Hertfordshire Partnership University NHS Foundation Trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11704.standard: NICE guidelines on managing non-cognitive symptoms of dementia (structured assessment, psychosocial interventions first, antipsychotics only if indicated, risk-benefit discussion, lowest dose, reassessment at 6 weeks)

cycle1.result: Structured assessment 55/55 (100%); psychosocial and environmental interventions offered 55/55 (100%); new antipsychotics in 7/55 (12.7%), all appropriate and at lowest effective dose; risk-benefit discussion documented 0/7 (0%); reassessment at 6 weeks documented in 4/19 (21%).

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11704.other_findings: 247 referrals screened; 12 of the 55 referrals were repeat referrals of 6 service users.

DOI:10.1136/archdischild-2019-nppc.38.topic: Sodium levels with heparin line flush solutions

cycle1.result: Mean admission sodium 139.96 mmol/L, 138 mmol/L at line removal or discharge (mean fall 2 mmol/L); 1 needed sodium supplementation; 2 lines blocked.

DOI:10.1136/archdischild-2019-nppc.38.intervention: Switch from heparin in sodium chloride 0.9% to heparin in sodium chloride 0.45% for arterial and CVP line flushes (cost saving), June 2018.

cycle2.result: Mean admission sodium 135.68 mmol/L, 135.72 mmol/L at line removal or discharge (mean change 0.04 mmol/L); 1 needed sodium supplementation; 2 lines blocked.

DOI:10.1136/archdischild-2019-nppc.38.other_findings: The 0.45% flush did not lower sodium levels; other sodium sources were not assessed.

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keab247.012.setting: Rheumatology services at 16 hospitals in northwest England (regional audit and survey)
DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keab247.012.standard: BSR guidance on giant cell arteritis (revised)

cycle1.result: 14/16 sites responded; 2 sites had a GCA pathway; routine steroid leaflets 6/14 (43%); 1 site had a GCA database; 8 had a steroid taper protocol.

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keab247.012.intervention: 2017 audit and survey results fed back to sites and regionally; sites introduced GCA pathways, temporal artery ultrasound, steroid leaflets and local QI.

cycle2.result: 15/16 sites responded; 6 sites had a GCA pathway; temporal artery ultrasound 6/15 (40%); routine steroid leaflets 12/15 (80%); GCA database 4 (27%); steroid taper protocol 7.

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keab247.012.other_findings: 9/15 (60%) sites said the 2017 audit prompted changes. No change in steroid card provision; 8/15 (53%) reported COVID-19 harmed services, mainly access to diagnostics.

DOI:10.1136/archdischild-2020-nppg.43.standard: 100% of positive m.1555A>G results recorded on prescribing record; 100% tested before aminoglycoside; 100% of positives not given an aminoglycoside

cycle1.result: 12 (0.31%) tested positive; 100% had the result recorded as an aminoglycoside allergy on JAC; 5/12 (42%) positives had received aminoglycosides, 1 before testing.

DOI:10.1136/archdischild-2020-nppg.43.other_findings: Unclear whether aminoglycoside use in positive patients was an informed risk-benefit decision; follow-up (including audiology) of these patients is being arranged.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znac404.083.setting: Hull Royal Infirmary; general surgery admissions during COVID-19
DOI:10.1093/bjs/znac404.083.standard: AUGIS guidance (March 2020) favouring conservative non-surgical management of acute cholecystitis during COVID-19

cycle1.result: Conservative management 15 (62.5%); percutaneous cholecystostomy 4 (16.6%); laparoscopic cholecystectomy 5 (20.8%). Mean stay 5.67 days; 30-day readmission 5 (20.8%).

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znac404.083.intervention: Initial audit presented at the general surgery clinical governance meeting in September 2020 as an educational intervention.

cycle2.result: Conservative management 22 (88%); percutaneous cholecystostomy 1 (4%); laparoscopic cholecystectomy 2 (8%). Mean stay 3.88 days; 30-day readmission 0 (0%).

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znac404.083.other_findings: Conservative management was not associated with complications such as empyema or perforation; two patients over 60 died of unrelated causes.

DOI:10.1136/archdischild-2023-nppg.35.setting: Tertiary NICU (ITU and HDU) with neonatal surgical service
DOI:10.1136/archdischild-2023-nppg.35.standard: NICE NG154 and local guidelines on indications and timing of standardised (NEON) PN (within 6 hours of life if <31+0 weeks) and on electrolyte and glucose corrections

cycle1.result: 11/11 correct indication; PN on time in 2/5 babies <31+0 weeks and 11/11 for other indications; electrolyte or glucose corrections per guideline 1/3; reasons for switching or stopping documented 11/11.

DOI:10.1136/archdischild-2023-nppg.35.other_findings: Delays attributed to night-time staff shortages for line insertion and lack of confidence giving peripheral PN; switches to bespoke PN were by consultants unfamiliar with NEON.

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keae163.046.setting: Doctor-led rheumatology clinics without obstetric input, University College London Hospital
DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keae163.046.standard: BSR 2022 guideline on prescribing drugs in pregnancy and breastfeeding (linked BSR audit tool)

cycle1.dates: Clinics 24 April to 30 April 2023; notes from preceding year
cycle1.result: Antibody screening 70%; asked about wish to conceive 26%; contraception asked in 21% of those not wishing to conceive; referred to obstetric-rheumatology clinic 17%; appropriate pre-pregnancy drug counselling 22.8% of 35 on medication; none signposted to further information.

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keae163.046.other_findings: 46% of patients without documented pre-pregnancy advice were taking medications unsafe in pregnancy. Audit to serve as baseline for a QI project.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11374.topic: Mental Health Act treatment form accuracy
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11374.setting: NHS Greater Glasgow and Clyde adult Community Mental Health Teams (five HSCPs)
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11374.standard: Mental Health (Care and Treatment) (Scotland) Act 2003 and Mental Welfare Commission guidance on T2B/T3B forms

cycle1.result: Forms and consent uploaded to EMIS 99.8%; clinic letters mentioning treatment orders 85%; referencing treatment forms 14%; medication matching forms 90%; GP Emergency Care Summary correspondence 80%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11374.other_findings: Clozapine was missing from ECS in two cases; discrepancies mainly from additional psychotropics and dose changes. Teams contacted and clinic letter format changed; re-audit planned in 12 months.

DOI:10.1136/gutjnl-2025-335134.setting: 147 UK hospitals; national prospective multicentre audit
DOI:10.1136/gutjnl-2025-335134.standard: Guideline adherence in AUGIB, notably pre-endoscopic risk stratification and restrictive transfusion thresholds

cycle1.result: Pre-endoscopic risk stratification not performed in 42%. Of early transfusions (38%), 43% given at Hb >70 g/L and 24% inappropriate due to haemodynamic stability. Inpatient endoscopy 83%; endotherapy 27%; rebleeding 9.7%; in-hospital mortality 8.8%; median stay 5 days.

DOI:10.1136/gutjnl-2025-335134.other_findings: Compared with the 2007 audit: transfusion 50% vs 43%, inpatient endoscopy 83% vs 74%, rebleeding 9.7% vs 13.3%, mortality 8.8% vs 10.0%. Inappropriate transfusion at 80 g/L was linked to higher adjusted mortality (aOR 1.60).

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10643.topic: VTE risk assessment in psychiatric inpatients
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10643.setting: Four acute psychiatric wards, St Ann's Hospital and Chase Farm Hospital (North London NHS Foundation Trust)
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10643.standard: Trust policy and Department of Health VTE risk assessment guidance

cycle1.result: VTE risk assessment done in 0/40 admissions.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10643.other_findings: Action plan: present at induction, share with consultants, nurses to check VTE assessment at clerking, and re-audit in 12 months.

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keag121.134.setting: National primary care prescribing dataset (ECLIPSE) linked to ophthalmology e-referrals across 32 Integrated Care Boards in England
DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keag121.134.standard: Royal College of Ophthalmologists guideline: annual retinopathy screening after 5 years of HCQ, or after 1 year if tamoxifen, eGFR <60 or dose >5 mg/kg/day

cycle1.dates: Prescriptions from 1 January 2016; data downloaded 28 August 2025
cycle1.result: Of 13,298 meeting screening criteria, 2,808 (21.1%) seen in ophthalmology in the previous 365 days; range 0% to 45.9% by ICB.

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keag121.134.other_findings: 52,419 patients prescribed HCQ; 5,338 on >5 mg/kg and 1,115 on >6.5 mg/kg. Rejected referrals and community optician attendance were not captured.

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/kead104.062.topic: Bosentan for digital ulcers in systemic sclerosis
DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/kead104.062.setting: Nurse-led Rapid Access to Digital Ulcer Clinic, Royal Free Hospital, London
DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/kead104.062.standard: NHS England clinical commissioning policy for sildenafil and bosentan in SSc digital ulceration (bosentan for severe vasculopathy or ≥3 digital ulcers; oral agents before IV prostanoids)

cycle1.result: All 21 had severe/≥3 digital ulcers; 20/21 started bosentan after inadequate response or intolerance to both sildenafil and iloprost. At 6 months (11/21), total ulcers fell from 5±2.2 to 2.7±2.2 (p < 0.05); 8/11 (72.7%) had fewer ulcers.

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/kead104.062.other_findings: Bosentan stopped in 3/21 in the first 6 months (2 liver function derangement, 1 non-compliance with monitoring), 2 restarted. More patients now start bosentan before IV prostanoids; to be audited in future.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.640.setting: Four Older Adult Community Mental Health Teams, Herefordshire and Worcestershire Health and Care NHS Trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.640.standard: Trust guideline: FBC, glucose, prolactin, U&E, lipids and LFTs every 6 months; HbA1c and clozapine plasma assay annually

cycle1.result: Full compliance: FBC 100%; HbA1c 100%; LFTs 71%; U&E 57%; clozapine level 43%; glucose 0%; prolactin 0%; lipids 0% (43% had at least one test).

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.640.other_findings: Many tests were done by GPs or hospitals for other reasons (e.g. 50% of U&Es, 71% of LFTs); authors suggest considering dedicated clozapine clinics.

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keag121.398.topic: Work loss risk in early inflammatory arthritis
DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keag121.398.setting: National Early Inflammatory Arthritis Audit cohort

cycle1.result: 168 (10.1%) reported work loss within three months. Predictors: age (IRR/decade 1.65), manual work (1.54), poor musculoskeletal health (1.55), anxiety/depression (1.45); final model C-statistic 0.708.

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keag121.398.other_findings: An 8-point risk score was developed; DAS28 >5.1 was not independently associated with work loss.

DOI:10.1136/archdischild-2022-nppg.23.topic: Prescribing errors in paediatric intensive care

cycle1.result: 36 pharmacist interventions: 92% per patient and 2.3% per prescription reviewed; 77.5% (n=31) related to intravenous medicines and 52.5% (n=21) to intravenous antibiotics.

DOI:10.1136/archdischild-2022-nppg.23.other_findings: Most errors were near misses on long day shifts; none with 15 or fewer items needed intervention. PDSA cycles planned towards a Trust target of 20% error reduction.

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keag121.249.setting: Therapies Department, East Kent Hospitals University NHS Foundation Trust
DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keag121.249.standard: CSP Musculoskeletal physiotherapy service standards (2022), MSK Core Capabilities Framework (2018), Rheumatology Physiotherapy Capabilities Framework (2021), CSP Quality Assurance Standards (2012), HCPC standards

cycle1.result: not reported

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keag121.249.other_findings: Describes development, piloting and external review of a documentation audit tool including 'asked and cleared' inflammatory and serious pathology screening; no audit results reported.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.402.setting: One adult male psychiatric intensive care unit and one adult female mental health ward
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.402.standard: Trust seclusion policy: reviews and documentation of commencement, periodic reviews and termination (target 100%)

cycle1.result: Rationale documented 100%; initial medical review within 1 hour 81.82% (27); 2-hourly nursing review 93.94% (31); 4-hourly medical review on time 24/33; 8-hour MDT consultant review 78.79% (26); physical health observations 100%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.402.other_findings: Delays in MDT review mainly when seclusion started at weekends or after hours. Recommendations: teaching, adding guidance to junior doctor handbook and induction, posters, and re-audit.

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keae163.052.topic: Uveitis screening in juvenile idiopathic arthritis
DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keae163.052.setting: Paediatric rheumatology clinic, Colchester General Hospital (district general hospital)

cycle1.result: Initial screen within 6 weeks 40/42 (95%); symptomatic seen within 1 week 4/13 (30%); screening after stopping DMARDs 9/13 (70%); ongoing screening 15/20 (75%).

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keae163.052.other_findings: Non-compliance was mainly due to unavailable ophthalmology appointments. After presentation, paediatric ophthalmology clinics increased to weekly, nurse specialist liaison and a shared database were introduced; re-audit planned.

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keaa111.006.topic: Psoriatic arthritis management against NICE NG65
DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keaa111.006.setting: Outpatient rheumatology clinic, Royal Berkshire Hospital, Reading
DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keaa111.006.standard: NICE NG65 spondyloarthritis guideline (NICE baseline assessment tool)

cycle1.result: CASPAR or peripheral ASAS criteria documented 78%; X-rays of symptomatic hands/feet 83%; information on PsA 58%; csDMARD monotherapy escalated 83%; flare advice access 100%; CV and skin cancer risk discussion on anti-TNF 30%.

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keaa111.006.other_findings: Action plan: best practice pathway on electronic patient records (CASPAR/ASAS, GRAPPA domains, CV and skin cancer risk) and nurse/therapist-led education sessions for all patients.

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keac133.137.topic: Calcium monitoring after denosumab in renal impairment
DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keac133.137.setting: Royal National Hospital for Rheumatic Diseases, Bath; secondary care
DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keac133.137.standard: Local protocol: weekly calcium and renal function for 4 weeks after each denosumab injection if CrCl <35 ml/min

cycle1.result: 29/52 (56%) missed one or more post-injection blood tests, most often the 1st and 4th weekly checks. 18/54 (33%) developed hypocalcaemia; only 3 had adjusted calcium <2.0 mmol/l.

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keac133.137.other_findings: Hypocalcaemia was generally mild, most often at 1 week, sometimes delayed to 4-6 weeks, and rarely needed treatment; CrCl did not differ between those with and without hypocalcaemia.

cycle1.result: 28% of concentrations within the therapeutic range.

DOI:10.1136/archdischild-2016-311535.56.intervention: Switch to continuous intravenous vancomycin infusion (loading dose 15 mg/kg then 20-50 mg/kg/day by creatinine and corrected gestational age), based on another hospital's regimen.

cycle2.result: 62% of 115 concentrations within range (60.8% first, 60% second, 65.6% subsequent); 71.3% within a 10% widened range.

DOI:10.1136/archdischild-2016-311535.56.other_findings: Comparator hospital achieved 77%; doses were prepared on the ward without aseptic facilities. Prefilled syringes and re-audit recommended.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znac404.181.setting: Tertiary referral centre, University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust
DOI:10.1093/bjs/znac404.181.standard: Local standard of routine feeding jejunostomy at oesophagectomy; literature morbidity 3-61%

cycle1.result: Any complication 81.8% (n=90); jejunostomy-specific complications 21.8% (n=24), commonest leak (44.8%); 4 major (Clavien-Dindo ≥III); no ischaemic small bowel necrosis (0.0% vs 3.74% in prior audit, p=0.029).

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znac404.181.other_findings: Re-audit planned July 2022 to July 2023 after departmental presentation. No at-risk population identified; ERAS warnings and electronic alerts on concurrent jejunostomy feed and inotropes are being introduced.

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keab247.002.topic: Vaccination uptake in immunosuppressed rheumatology patients
DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keab247.002.setting: Rheumatology outpatient clinics, Salford Royal Hospital
DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keab247.002.standard: Public Health England, BSR and EULAR vaccination guidance; target 90% uptake; departmental vaccination advice in standard letter template

cycle1.result: Influenza 63/87 (72%); pneumococcus 61/87 (70%); zoster 7/12 (64%); vaccination advice in 24/126 (19%) clinic letters.

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keab247.002.other_findings: 22 of 109 had no vaccination status in GP records. Planned: writing to patients about influenza vaccination, changing the letter template, and re-audit.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11839.setting: Psychiatry department inpatients, Gulab Devi Teaching Hospital, Lahore
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11839.standard: Recommended baseline physical, laboratory and additional investigations before starting atypical antipsychotics

cycle1.result: Weight/BMI 64%; blood pressure 28%; waist 0%; CBC 56%; LFTs and RFTs 52%; glucose/HbA1c 44%; lipids 48%; CPK and prolactin 0%; ECG 40%; pregnancy test 0. Combined compliance about 29%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11839.intervention: Staff education, standardised baseline investigation checklists, visual reminders and better coordination with laboratory and ECG services.

cycle2.result: Weight/BMI 68%; blood pressure 76%; waist 48%; CBC 100%; LFTs 88%; RFTs 84%; glucose/HbA1c 76%; lipids 60%; CPK 48%; prolactin 60%; ECG 68%; pregnancy test 88%. Combined compliance 68%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11839.other_findings: Physical assessments improved from 30.7% to 64%, laboratory from 36% to 76.6% and additional investigations from 20% to 62% over a two-month prospective audit.

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keaf142.249.topic: Glycaemic monitoring in giant cell arteritis on steroids
DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keaf142.249.setting: Fast Track GCA pathway, University College London Hospital
DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keaf142.249.standard: BSR GCA guideline: baseline HbA1c within two weeks of steroid start; wean steroids within 18 months

cycle1.result: Baseline HbA1c 32 (69.57%); HbA1c at least 3 months after starting steroids 36 (78.26%); both baseline and follow-up by rheumatology 17/46 (36.96%); steroids weaned within 18 months 31 (67.39%).

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keaf142.249.other_findings: A simple glucocorticoid-induced diabetes algorithm was developed with endocrinology for use in clinic.

DOI:10.1136/archdischild-2017-314584.50.topic: Uveitis screening in juvenile idiopathic arthritis
DOI:10.1136/archdischild-2017-314584.50.setting: Paediatric tertiary centre and satellite clinics (Childhood Arthritis Prospective Study patients)
DOI:10.1136/archdischild-2017-314584.50.standard: BSPAR/RCO uveitis screening guidelines (screen within 6 weeks of referral); NHS England JIA treatment recommendations

cycle1.result: Referred for screening 50/54 (92.6%); screened 45/50 (90%); screened within 6 weeks of referral 8/45 (17.8%); JIA treatment in line with NHS England 100% of 41 documented.

DOI:10.1136/archdischild-2017-314584.50.other_findings: 4/45 (8.9%) diagnosed with uveitis. Recommendations: better communication with satellite clinics and training for junior staff on screening targets.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znac248.098.topic: MRCP use in suspected biliary disease
DOI:10.1093/bjs/znac248.098.setting: Beaumont Hospital, Dublin; major teaching hospital
DOI:10.1093/bjs/znac248.098.standard: BSG gallstone guidelines used as an adjunct

cycle1.result: 82 inpatient and 9 outpatient MRCPs; mean inpatient wait 3.2 days; ultrasound before MRCP in 41 (45%); CBD stones found in 15 (16%); 20 (22%) had surgical biliary decompression.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znac248.098.other_findings: Recommendation to develop a hospital guideline with radiology and gastroenterology.
